$comment: What each shipped locale actually CLAIMS, who stands behind it, and when that claim expires.
P2.2 in specs/readiness-recovery-10-10/tasks.md.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The app registers nine languages and ships strings for one. `ckb.json` is
literally `{}` — zero Kurdish strings — and `i18n/index.ts` sets `lng: "ckb"`, so Kurdish is the
DEFAULT language. With `fallbackLng: "en"` every string resolves to English, silently, and the
interface a Kurdish-first product presents to a Kurdish learner is entirely English.
Nothing said so. `tests/i18n/locale-parity.test.mjs` checks that every key in a locale is
well-formed, and an EMPTY locale satisfies every one of those rules vacuously: no key can carry a
dropped interpolation variable, or be identical to the English, or be an empty string, if there
is no key. The gate was green because there was nothing to check, which is not the same as being
right.
This file makes the claim explicit so a test can hold the code to it, and so a human reading one
file can see what is real. `reviewer: null` is not a placeholder to be tidied away — it is the
statement that NOBODY has reviewed these strings, which is exactly what P2.4 asks for and does
not have.
STATUSES
complete     every English key is present, reviewed by a named person, not expired.
partial      some keys present and reviewed; the rest fall back to English by design.
placeholder  registered so the language can be SELECTED, with no strings behind it. Everything
the user sees is English. Offering it is a product decision, not a translation.
The tests in tests/i18n/locale-parity.test.mjs assert this file against the locale files
themselves, in BOTH directions: a locale claiming more coverage than it has fails, and so does
one claiming less. A manifest that can drift from the thing it describes is decoration.

en.reviewer: source language — authored here, not translated

ckb.note: Central Kurdish (Sorani). The app's DEFAULT language and an option in the language picker, with zero strings. Every label a Kurdish learner sees is English via fallback. P2.4 covers getting these written and independently reviewed, including Quranic terminology; until then this row is the honest description of the product.
